messages.author: 8c45483022d450d5
messages.subject: Re: Can "seasonal STAR" model fit into the function"predict{tsDyn}"?
parts:
Hi

As discussed previously in a similar post, tsDyn does not allow for exogeneous regressors, see:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/tsdyn/ts-FZgL6D8E

If you were to modify lstar() yourself, you should modify several lines, the most important being 85 and 86:
xxL <- cbind(const,xx[,1:mL])

then add your regressors. YOu will need probably to modify the code at several other places, to take into account the fact that you have more regressors, hence parameter naming might fail. You will in any case not be able to use the predict() since the predict use a loop starting from zero to re-create the series. This would require significant changes.

Good luck

PS: copying to the mailing list for archiving, and to Anzor who asked a similar question.

Matthieu



2013/8/23 危黎黎 <we...@hubu.edu.cn>

Dear prof Matthieu,

    As a R program beginner ,I want to extend the STAR model codes based on your “tsDyn” package. Firstly,I would like to express my great appreciation for you and your team work.

    If I add four seasonal dummy variables D[1,t]、D[2,t]、D[3,t] and D[4,t] with time varying function G2(t*,gamma2,th2) into STAR model, that is

  x[t]=(phi1[0]+phi1[1]x[t-1]+….phi1[mL]x[t-mL])
+(phi2[0]+phi2[1] x[t-1]+….phi2[mH]x[t-mH])G(z[t],gamma,th)
+(a1[1]D[1,t]+a1[2]D[2,t]+a1[3]D[3,t]+a1[4]D[4,t])
+(a2[1]D[1,t]+a2[2]D[2,t]+ a2[3]D[3,t]+ a2[4]D[4,t]) G2(t*,gamma2,th2)

where the t*=1/T,2/T,.......,T/T.

Please tell me if the above “seasonal smooth transition” model can use the“predict{tsDyn}” function?If not,can you give me some advice for solve this problem?
    Thanks a lot.I am looking forward to hearing from you .All the best!

                                                                                                                  Sincerely ,Wei Lili
